title: Quantum n-coloring is undecidable for every n $\ge$ 3
authors: Christian Bo Kidmose-Frederiksen, Alfred Leth Nielsen
abstract: The quantum $n$-coloring problem, given graph $G$, asks whether there exists a perfect quantum strategy for the $n$-coloring game of $G$. Previously it was known that quantum $n$-coloring is undecidable only for $n=3$. We extend this to all $n\geq 3$ with one elementary reduction. Letting $G'=(G\square K_3)\lor K_{n-3}$, we show that $G$ is quantum $3$-colorable if and only if $G'$ is quantum $n$-colorable.
summary: This paper proves that determining whether a graph can be quantum n-colored is an undecidable problem for any number of colors n greater than or equal to 3. The authors achieve this by constructing a specific related graph G' and showing that the quantum 3-coloring problem can be reduced to the quantum n-coloring problem via this construction. This result significantly expands the known boundaries of decidability in quantum graph theory.
main_problem: The paper addresses the decidability of the quantum n-coloring problem for an arbitrary graph G, which asks if a perfect quantum strategy exists for the n-coloring game.
main_result: The authors prove that for every fixed integer n greater than or equal to 3, the quantum n-coloring decision problem is undecidable.
method: They establish a reduction from the known undecidable case of quantum 3-coloring to the general case using a specific graph construction: G' = (G <0xE2><0xA8><0x81> K_3) <0xE2><0xA8><0x81> K_{n-3}.
